certainty_reasoning: Wood's sworn testimony: he lived at Taylor's Little College Street rooms for about three weeks in January 1893, sleeping 'in the same room with Taylor. There was only one bed there,' and in re-examination he dated his first acts of indecency 'with any man' to going to College Street. The landlady corroborates the three-week stay. But no witness states an act with Taylor himself; no charge of indecency between them was ever put to a jury (Taylor's Wood counts were for procuring, and ended in a directed not-guilty); and Taylor dated their meeting differently (May 1892, at Atkins's rooms). Strong implication, no attestation → 'alleged'.
date_label: January 1893 (three weeks' cohabitation; acquaintance possibly from May 1892 per Taylor)
summary: Alfred Wood, an out-of-work clerk, lived at Taylor's one-bed rooms at 13 Little College Street for about three weeks in January 1893, sharing the room and — on the arithmetic of his own testimony that the rooms held 'only one bed' — the bed. He dated his first acts of indecency to going to College Street without naming a partner. Taylor said they had met earlier, in May 1892 at Atkins's rooms. The procuring-Wood counts against Taylor ended in a directed not-guilty; no count alleged acts between the two men.

disputed.claim: that sexual relations occurred between Taylor and Wood at 13 Little College Street, January 1893
disputed.asserted_by: the implication of Wood's own sworn testimony (a single bed shared for three weeks; first acts of indecency dated to 'when I went to College Street' — Hyde pp. 201, 205)
disputed.disputed_by: no direct attestation by any witness; no charge concerning acts between Taylor and Wood; the counts charging Taylor with procuring Wood for Wilde ended in a directed verdict of Not Guilty (Hyde pp. 292-293)
disputed.grounds: testimony implies but never states acts with Taylor himself; classification per the single-source/contested rule

sources.quote: Alfred Wood, examined by Mr. Avory—I was formerly a clerk. In January, 1893, I was not in any occupation. I first knew Taylor about that time. When did you go to Little College Street to live?—In January, 1893. I stayed about three weeks. Where did you sleep there?—In the same room with Taylor. There was only one bed there.
sources.context: Alfred Wood's examination-in-chief, Regina v. Wilde and Taylor, 26 April 1895
sources.supports: the three-week single-bed cohabitation, January 1893 — the class-deciding quote
